newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling slips in mixed trading.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling slips in mixed trading.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling slipped further on Tuesday in mixed trading as panic dollar buying to cover small short positions soaked up dollars offloaded by commercial banks' clients, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 54.71 against the dollar from 54.66 on Monday, while against the pound it was posted at 91.24 from 90.97.
Dealers said the shilling was struggling to pick up amid intervention from the central bank.
"The central bank was here in the morning buying at 54.70," one commercial bank dealer said. "It appears the bank does not want it to go beyond that level."

On Monday, a dealer said he did not see the shilling weakening in the long term as a lot of the demand seen was to cover short positions brought forward from December and not because of strategic buying.
But some dealers said they expected the shilling to recoup some of its losses on inflows from the agricultural sector.
The money market was tight with rates quoted above 25 percent. Dealers said banks sought funds to cover payments for matured treasury bills due on Tuesday.
